A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the common genetic variants in UMOD gene promoter are associated with increased expression of uromoduline, which leads to salt-sensitive hypertension, kidney damage and CKD.
the UMOD gene encodes a protein called uromodulin that is secreted into the urine and that this protein has a role in regulating the kidney's ability to excrete sodium.
common noncoding UMOD genetic variants cause salt-sensitive hypertension and CKD by inducing uromodulin overproduction, which in turn increases renal salt reabsorption and causes kidney damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
common genetic variants that cause increased expression of uromoduline are a major cause of hypertension and chronic kidney disease.
uromodulin can be used as a target for therapeutic intervention in hypertension and CKD.
uromodulin is a key regulator of salt homeostasis in the kidney.
